name: es32-layered-rendering
title: Layered rendering: gl_Layer, cube map in one pass
summary: glFramebufferTexture attaches whole levels of a 2D array, a 3D and a cube map texture (layered attachments) and geometry shaders pick the layer with gl_Layer: four POINTS paint four array layers (layer = gl_PrimitiveIDIn), one point with layout(invocations = 4) paints four 3D slices (gl_InvocationID), and a room of walls, decals and boxes is rendered into all six cube map faces in ONE draw call (invocations = 6, per-face view-projection, gl_Layer = gl_InvocationID, the fragment shader reads gl_Layer back). The cube map is shown as a mirror ball in its own room (reflect() + skybox) and as a cube net. Every layer is read back through glFramebufferTextureLayer / glFramebufferTexture2D and compared byte for byte with a CPU model (a ray caster for the cube map, which also proves the face orientation of Table 8.19); FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_LAYERED / TEXTURE_LAYER queries, the INCOMPLETE_LAYER_TARGETS rules, the errors of glFramebufferTexture*, and the gl_Layer rules the specification defines (default layer 0, clear touches all layers, ReadPixels reads layer 0, ignored by a non-layered framebuffer, EndPrimitive between layers, the provoking vertex) are checked.
spec: ES 3.2 §9.2.8 Attaching Texture Images to a Framebuffer (FramebufferTexture, FramebufferTexture2D, FramebufferTextureLayer, §9.2.8.1 Effects of Attaching a Texture Image), §9.2.2.1 Layered Images
ES 3.2 §9.2.3 Framebuffer Object Queries (FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_LAYERED, TEXTURE_LAYER, OBJECT_NAME, TEXTURE_LEVEL), §9.2.1 (FRAMEBUFFER_DEFAULT_LAYERS)
ES 3.2 §9.4.1 Framebuffer Attachment Completeness, §9.4.2 Whole Framebuffer Completeness (FRAMEBUFFER_INCOMPLETE_LAYER_TARGETS)

ES 3.2 §9.8 Layered Framebuffers (layer number, undefined out-of-range layers, Clear and ReadPixels, cube map layers 0..5), §11.3.4.5 Layer Selection (LAYER_PROVOKING_VERTEX), §11.3.4.2 Instanced Geometry Shaders
ES 3.2 §8.13 / Table 8.19 Cube Map Texture Selection and Table 8.24 (layer -> face), §8.14 Texture Completeness, Table 21.40 (MAX_FRAMEBUFFER_LAYERS, MAX_ARRAY_TEXTURE_LAYERS)

GLSL ES 3.20 §7.1.4 Geometry Shader Special Variables (gl_Layer), §7.1.5 Fragment Shader Special Variables (gl_Layer input), §4.4.1 / §4.4.2 Geometry Inputs and Outputs, §8.9 Texture Lookup Functions (texelFetch, texture on samplerCube)

api.glFramebufferTexture: attaches whole levels of a 2D array, a 3D and a cube map texture (and a cube depth texture): FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_LAYERED is TRUE for all three, FALSE for a plain 2D texture; the attachments are rendered into by geometry shaders (every layer compared); completeness COMPLETE alone and with a layered depth, INCOMPLETE_LAYER_TARGETS beside a non-layered renderbuffer, a non-layered or a different-target colour attachment; errors: default framebuffer bound, name that is not a texture, level 1 of a 1-level texture and level -1 -> INVALID_VALUE (INVALID_OPERATION for the default framebuffer); texture 0 detaches
api.glFramebufferTextureLayer: attaches one layer of a 2D array / 3D texture: LAYERED FALSE, TEXTURE_LAYER = layer, read back for every layer of the array, the 3D texture and the semantic tests; a non-layered framebuffer ignores gl_Layer; layer = layer count -> FRAMEBUFFER_INCOMPLETE_ATTACHMENT; layer = MAX_ARRAY_TEXTURE_LAYERS or -1 -> INVALID_VALUE, a plain 2D texture -> INVALID_OPERATION; on a cube map Mesa accepts the call without effect (XFAIL)
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: cube map faces (TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP_POSITIVE_X + layer) read back texel by texel and compared with the ray-cast of the room; plain 2D texture: LAYERED FALSE; TEXTURE_2D with the name of a 2D array texture -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glFramebufferRenderbuffer: a depth renderbuffer beside a layered colour attachment makes the framebuffer INCOMPLETE_LAYER_TARGETS; beside a non-layered one it is COMPLETE
api.glCheckFramebufferStatus: COMPLETE / INCOMPLETE_LAYER_TARGETS / INCOMPLETE_ATTACHMENT / INCOMPLETE_MISSING_ATTACHMENT for sixteen framebuffer configurations (every layered / non-layered / mixed combination of the specification's two LAYER_TARGETS rules, each with a control, the demo's own framebuffers, an attachment-less one)
api.glGetFramebufferAttachmentParameteriv: OBJECT_TYPE, OBJECT_NAME, TEXTURE_LEVEL, TEXTURE_LAYER and FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_LAYERED for eight attachment kinds
api.glFramebufferParameteri: FRAMEBUFFER_DEFAULT_LAYERS = 5 on an attachment-less framebuffer (read back, COMPLETE); > MAX_FRAMEBUFFER_LAYERS and negative -> INVALID_VALUE with the old value kept
api.glGetFramebufferParameteriv: FRAMEBUFFER_DEFAULT_LAYERS initial value 0 and after the call
api.glTexStorage3D: 64x64x4 RGBA8 2D array and 3D textures and an 8x8x4 array: the layered render targets (immutable, one level)
api.glTexStorage2D: RGBA8 and DEPTH_COMPONENT24 cube maps (6 layers each) and small 2D textures
api.glTexParameteri: NEAREST filters so the immutable textures are complete for texelFetch
api.glSamplerParameteri: filters/wraps: NEAREST for the cube net (exact texels), LINEAR for the mirror ball and skybox (equal texels blend to the same colour)
api.glBindSampler: unit 0 uses the sampler instead of the texture's own filter state; both looks compared with the CPU model
api.glClearBufferfv: clears colour (all layers) and depth of the layered environment framebuffer; after a clear all four layers of the semantic-test texture read back as the clear colour
api.glDrawArrays: 4 POINTS (layer = gl_PrimitiveIDIn), 1 POINT with four invocations, the environment triangle list with six invocations, full-screen triangles for the tiles, the sky, and the semantic tests
api.glDrawElements: the mirror ball (96 x 48 UV sphere); observed through reflection probes
api.glUniformMatrix4fv: six view-projection matrices (array of 6 in the geometry shader) for the six faces: every face texel equals the CPU ray-cast, so the matrices and the face numbering are right; preview matrices
api.glUniform2i: tile origin in the tile shaders (every pixel of the array and volume tiles equals the layer image)
api.glUniform1i: layer / slice / face selection of the tile shaders
api.glUniform3f: eye position of the sky and the ball
api.glUniform4f: solid colour of the semantic-test fragment shader
api.glReadPixels: every layer of the three layered textures (64x64 each) and the default framebuffer; reads layer 0 of a layered framebuffer
api.glReadBuffer: COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 of the read framebuffer holding one layer
api.glGetIntegerv: MAX_FRAMEBUFFER_LAYERS >= 256, MAX_ARRAY_TEXTURE_LAYERS >= 256, LAYER_PROVOKING_VERTEX (one of FIRST/LAST/UNDEFINED; the provoking-vertex test is chosen from it)
api.glGenFramebuffers: layered framebuffers for the array, the volume and the cube, a scratch read framebuffer, completeness test framebuffers
api.glBindTexture: creates the textures, binds the cube map for the sky, ball and net, the array and 3D texture for the tiles
api.glGenRenderbuffers: DEPTH_COMPONENT24 renderbuffer of the completeness test
api.glScissor: per-cell and per-tile clipping (the unused corners of the cube net keep the clear colour)
api.glEnable: DEPTH_TEST for the environment pass (hidden surfaces of the boxes) and the ball; SCISSOR_TEST
api.glGenBuffers: environment vertex buffer (positions + colours), sphere vertices and indices
api.glGenVertexArrays: environment, sphere and an empty VAO for gl_VertexID draws

visual_review.notes: Viewed the gpu, llvmpipe and zink es-max captures (256x256, identical to the eye). Top left: a glass-like mirror ball inside a room corner (teal wall on the left, purple wall behind, an ochre box at the bottom) that reflects the whole room: orange wall, green wall with an orange stripe, a white lamp, a yellow window, red and blue boxes, with a bright rim at the edge. Top right: the cube net on a dark gray background: light-gray ceiling with a white lamp on top, then teal wall with a dark-blue door, green wall with an orange stripe, orange-red wall with a yellow window and a purple wall with a teal poster in the middle row, dark floor with a red carpet and the three boxes at the bottom; the four corners of the net are empty. Bottom left: four 64x64 tiles, dark red / dark green on the bottom row and dark blue / dark purple on the top row, each with a body square that shrinks (red, green, blue, orange) and one to four white squares along the bottom edge (layer 0 bottom left, layer 3 top right). Bottom right: four tiles with a background that goes from blue to green, a yellow block walking up the diagonal and an orange bar that grows from 16 to 64 pixels.
